excerpt: Table 1 lists the sketch-generation rules used by Ansor: Skip, AlwaysInline, Multi-levelTiling, Multi-levelTilingwithFusion, AddCacheStage, and ReductionFactorization. The surrounding text states that sketches represent high-level structures while annotations hold low-level choices such as tile size, parallelism, unrolling, and vectorization.
overview: The rule table is concrete evidence for Ansor's hierarchical search-space claim. It shows how the system automatically constructs candidate high-level structures from a computation graph instead of requiring a hand-written template for each operator. The evidence also limits the claim: the listed rules are those used for CPU examples, while GPU support uses additional target-specific derivations.
title: Sketch Derivation Rule Table
